text:
alex: quick follow-up from the RFC — proposing a per-route claim slimdown for service tokens. idea: tokens only carry `route_id` + minimal actor scope (verb set), and we surface org/project context via a separate signed header so we don't bloat tokens. small perf + observability wins.

mira: short question — is this for both svc->svc and external API keys? :thinking_face:

alex: primary target is svc->svc (internal proxies + gateway). external API keys we can keep richer claims for now for backwards compat. goal is to make internal routing decisions cheap and cache-friendly.

ben: how do we handle rare cases where per-route needs richer role lists (eg. dynamic admin checks)?

alex: two options: 1) stable fallback: runtime can call authz service for expanded claims on demand (cold path), or 2) route-level metadata in the route registry that indicates "needs-expanded-claims" and the gateway requests a short-lived expanded token. tradeoffs: (1) keeps runtime simple but adds authz calls; (2) more tooling around route registry + token minting.

ravi: +1 for keeping the hot path tiny. curious about auditing — separating org/project header means audit trail needs correlation keys. we should include a lightweight correlation id in both token and header.

alex: agreed. proposal: token payload minimal, header includes `X-RW-Org`, `X-RW-Project`, and `X-RW-Corr-Id`. example token payload:

```
{
  "sub": "svc:billing-internal",
  "route_id": "bill:v2:get-invoice",
  "verbs": ["read"],
  "exp": 1710000000
}
```

and header example: `X-RW-Org: org_12345`, `X-RW-Project: proj_88`, `X-RW-Corr-Id: r-abc123`

mira: for the expanded token flow, can we reuse the existing ephemeral minting service? I don't want a new PKI surface.

alex: yup reuse minting service. it already supports short TTLs and audit hooks. just need a new mint endpoint `mint/expanded-claims` that takes `route_id` + corr id.

ben: any impact on caching at the gateway? we should be explicit: cached auth decision keyed by (route_id, actor_id, corr_id?) corr_id should not be part of cache key. use (route_id, actor_id, token_version).

alex: good call. we'll document `token_version` bump when we change shape. cache key = (route_id, actor_id, token_version). corr id only for logs.

ravi: security thought: separating org/project in headers means proxies must assert header immutability (no client-supplied override). gateway must strip any inbound `X-RW-*` headers from external requests. Also require mTLS or signed upstream.

alex: yep policy: strip inbound `X-RW-*`, require mTLS between internal components. the gateway will validate header signature against KMS.

mira: rollout plan? we need gradual opt-in per service to avoid breaking legacy services that parse full claims.

alex: rollout: (a) implement header support + mint endpoint; (b) introduce token_version v2 and mint both v1/v2 simultaneously; (c) run dual-validate in gateway where it accepts either full claims or v2 header+minimal token; (d) service teams opt-in and then we deprecate v1 after 3 months.

ben: can we add a short lint in sdk to warn when code depends on full-role lists inside tokens? that would speed migrations.

alex: yes will add a dep-checker in the node/py SDKs that flags `token.roles` access.

security-bot: Created follow-up ticket RWINF-3245 and thread RFC-FOLLOWUP-2026. Link: https://tickets.redwood.example/RWINF-3245

mira: thanks — will post a short RFC summary + migration checklist in #eng-architectures tomorrow. :thumbsup:

alex: thanks all. next step: I'll draft the mint endpoint spec and route registry flags and share a short PR for review.
